chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Abdillah al-Farra', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from our companions said to him: 'Sometimes the prayer time is confused for us on a cloudy day.' So he said: 'Do you know those birds which are with you in Iraq that are called roosters?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'When their calls rise and respond to each other, then the sun has declined,' — or he said: 'Then pray it.'

key_terms.الديكة: Roosters (plural of ديك), used here as a natural indicator of solar noon
key_terms.الوقت: Prayer time, specifically the determined time for each of the five daily prayers
key_terms.زالت الشمس: The sun's declination past the meridian — the canonical marker for the start of Dhuhr prayer time

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Sadiq determine prayer time on cloudy days?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provided a practical method for determining the time of the noon prayer (Dhuhr) on cloudy days when the sun is not directly visible. He directed the questioner to use the crowing of roosters as a natural timekeeper — specifically, when roosters raise their calls and crow in succession, this indicates that the sun has passed its zenith and the time for Dhuhr prayer has begun. This ruling addressed a real concern for the Imam's companions in Iraq, where cloudy weather could make it difficult to observe the sun's position.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Abdullah Al Fara’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘A man from our companions said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes the time is doubtful upon us during the cloudy day. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you know these birds which are with you at Al-Iraq, called the rooster?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it raises its voice and is responded to, so the sun has (started to) decline’, or said: ‘So pray it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu ‘Abd Allah, al-Farra’ who has said the following:

“A man from our people once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘In a cloudy day sometimes the identifying the exact time becomes confusing.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Are you aware of the existence of these birds, in Iraq, called al-Dikah (rooster)?’ He (the man) replied, ‘Yes, I am aware.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘When they raise their voices and others respond, it is the time when the sun declines toward the west at noontime, or that he (the Imam) said, ‘You must perform Salah (prayer).”’
